what: Today's CI (.github/workflows/check.yaml), which tests next/ and the tooling, was too slow and cost too much for anything to land, so the owner called a sev0 on 2026-11-14. The first measure, ci-speed.ts at 2026-11-14 21:40 UTC over the last 24 hours (experiment 293), gave in minutes, median and worst 10%: pull request checks 15.4 and 58.0, merge queue 52.5 and 167.2, last push to merged 28.2 and 219.7, with 87% of the 20 runners busy. Experiment 291 counted 300 check runs from 07:40 to 20:38 UTC: 15,057 machine-minutes, of which the merge queue took 6,937 (46%), and 49 of its 85 groups failed. One red group made every group behind it run again. The freeze emptied the queue and canceled runs; the fixes landed one at a time (decision 0532). The last fixes merged at 01:58 UTC on 2026-11-15, and from then the merge line ran normally with fixes first. The owner ended the sev0 at about 04:18 UTC, once decision 0542 named that state a sev1. By then a full run had opened a ci-scheduled issue, so CI is now in a sev1.
cause: The merge queue ran the full suite on every group, so one red group reran every group behind it; next/'s generated laws over real SQLite, git, workerd and browsers took 66% of next/'s test time (experiment 291); pull requests and the queue also ran today's version's tests and every tooling test; and no rule said what to do while CI itself was the emergency.
fix: Two scheduled checks now watch CI with nobody asking: the 3-hour full run opens a ci-scheduled issue when main is red (0534), and the daily speed check opens one when a stage is over 0541's goal. An open issue is a sev1 (0542), so the next slowdown is caught before it needs a sev0.
test: The daily ci-speed.ts reading keeps every stage inside 0541's goal (3 and 5, 3 and 5, 8 and 15 minutes), and a green 3-hour full run on main closes issue 1297.
levels: sev0, today's CI. Start: the owner's call earlier on 2026-11-14; no public record holds its minute. The freeze emptied the merge queue at about 20:15 UTC, when its last three groups were canceled, and no group ran again until 22:44 UTC. Decision 0532, the rule, merged at 20:53 UTC. The first rule that day let the queue drain; it did not work, because one red entry reran every entry behind it, and the owner changed it to 0532.
sev0 by its own rule, end: 2026-11-15 01:58 UTC, when pull requests 1290 and 1289, the last fixes, merged. From 01:59 UTC the merge line ran normally with fixes first.
sev0 in name, end: 2026-11-15 about 04:18 UTC, when the owner said yes. Decision 0542 merged at 04:23 UTC, a few minutes after; the sev skill (pull request 1257) was written but not yet merged.

sev1, start: 2026-11-15 04:22 UTC, when the second full run, 43676389337, opened issue 1297. It is still open as this is written. The run went red outside any test: Playwright's Chromium install in leg next (e2e-2) failed with exit code 100, and the first red job stopped the run.
fixes: 1243, 20:34 UTC: CI setup gets an incremental typecheck, blobless history, no pnpm store cache (ticket 974).
1256, 20:55 UTC: the first red job stops its run on a pull request or in the queue (ticket 990).
1241, 21:39 UTC: each next/ leg starts its heaviest test file first (ticket 972).
1263, 21:48 UTC: CI runs no test of today's version (0533, ticket 995).
1253, 22:11 UTC: a pull request of only plan files and field rows starts no CI run (ticket 988).
1266, 22:56 UTC: the queue and main run only the next/ tests a change reaches, and a schedule runs all every 3 hours (0534, ticket 997).
1277, 23:22 UTC: the leak check reads a line moved between files as old text.
1270, 23:30 UTC: git gets an in-memory test layer for next/'s repository laws (ticket 999).
1278, 23:50 UTC: real-resource and visual tests leave pull requests and the queue, by file name (0536, ticket 1001).
1281, 00:49 UTC: pnpm lint runs its 17 parts at once (ticket 1005). It merged in the window and cuts the lint job; whether it was on the fix list is not recorded.
1283, 01:01 UTC: a queue group whose trees a ready pull request run already tested green runs no tests (experiment 292). Merged in the window; whether it was on the fix list is not recorded.
1287, 01:38 UTC: a lockfile, tsconfig, package.json or shard table change runs only the tests it reaches.
1282, 01:46 UTC: every test leg writes a time table (ticket 1006).
1286, 01:51 UTC: the typecheck lock laws use their own lock file, so a real typecheck no longer turns them red (ticket 1008).
1290, 01:58 UTC: next/'s merge line legs fit a 240 second budget (ticket 997).
1289, 01:58 UTC: pull requests and the queue run no tooling test (0539, ticket 1010).

After the turn: 1291 (decision 0541, the goal) at 02:30 UTC; 1268 (the daily speed check, experiment 293, ticket 998) at 02:49 UTC; 1293 (ticket 1022) at 03:29 UTC; 1295 (ticket 1024) at 04:06 UTC; 1296 (ticket 1023) at 04:13 UTC; 1298 (decision 0542, ticket 1025) at 04:23 UTC.
after: ci-speed.ts's own code, run over 01:59 to 03:18 UTC on 2026-11-15 with 15 pull requests merged: pull request checks 2.8 and 3.8 minutes, merge queue 3.0 and 3.7, and 22% of 20 runners busy against 87% before. Last push to merged was 7.2 and 12.1 over the 12 changes whose last push came after the turn. Over all 15 it is 8.5 and 306.0, because three pull requests (1250, 1260, 1267) were last pushed hours before and waited through the freeze. The queue's median sits on the goal's edge: ci-speed.ts marks 3.0 as over, since it is a little above 3.
cost: Runner time: 15,057 machine-minutes in the 13 hours experiment 291 counted, before most of the freeze; 6,937 of them in the queue, where 49 of 85 groups failed. Waiting: 90 runs created from 20:00 to 02:00 UTC ended canceled (63 pull request runs on 33 branches, 24 push runs on main, 3 queue groups); some were canceled by a newer push, not the freeze. No dollar figure is in experiments 291 to 293. The runners are GitHub's hosted ones on a public repository, which GitHub lists as free, but no bill was read. Not measured: the agent dollars of the day, and the hours of work that stopped while every other agent saved and waited.
learned: The level. By 0532's own words the sev0 should have ended when its fixes merged, at 01:58 UTC. It stayed open in name for about two and a half more hours, because no second level existed for 'fixes go first, the rest lands'. That gap is why 0542 was written. A sev0 that ends needs a level to land in.

A full run is the only proof of a fix now. The first full run, 43673342835, started by hand at 03:39 UTC because no schedule event had yet fired in the repository, found one real-resource law red on main: L1 in next/packages/libfabrika/src/node/ProgramMailReads.integration.test.ts, a test setup fault that pull request 1226 brought in and that merged without it, since real-resource tests no longer run on pull requests (0536). Pull request 1295 fixed it (ticket 1024).

That same run opened no issue, because its failing leg ended cancelled once the first red job stopped the run. Pull request 1296 fixed the report (ticket 1023), and the second full run proved it by opening issue 1297.

The rename in pull request 1278 left one visual law starting its child run with two old file names. Nothing showed it for hours, because visual tests no longer run on pull requests (ticket 1022, pull request 1293).
After that rename GitHub marked pull requests as conflicting that a local merge resolved; the sev skill (pull request 1257) records this, and no other record of it was found.

A rerun tests old code. Run 43672758072, a fresh run after a draft-then-ready flip at 03:31 UTC, checked out a merge of ddf230258 into 93fc2e4f4, a main from 02:49 UTC, when main was already 80cb1bc15. So leaving a sev0 now reruns nothing (0542).

The owner had to ask the lead for every number all day, so the lead built a status page by hand; the scenario for doing it in the product is docs/direction/scenario-watch-ci-in-a-workspace.md (pull request 1284, ticket 1009).
One test, the Project entry-flow law, timed out once at 60 s on a leg that ran about 6 times slower than every other (ticket 1021, finding row in pull request 1294).
unknown: This note cannot tell: the minute the owner called the sev0; what the agent hours or dollars of the day were; how many hours of work stopped; which of the runs canceled in the window the freeze canceled and which a newer push did, since no log of the day's cancel loop was found; or whether the speed holds on a normal day, since the 'after' reading covers only 79 minutes and 15 changes. It has no summary printed by the sev skill's close command, because none was found: the day's cancel loop ran in the lead's session, and the sev skill (pull request 1257) is not merged yet.
